content.title: About
content.content: A sweet cinnamon roll is a soft yeasted dough swirled with a fragrant cinnamon filling and served without frosting. It is a classic treat in Scandinavian and American cuisines, often enjoyed with tea or coffee.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original cinnamon roll, called kanelbulle, originated in Sweden.
In the United States, National Cinnamon Roll Day is celebrated on October 4th.
The dough is typically made with milk, butter, and eggs, giving it a tender, airy texture.
The filling usually contains ground cinnamon, sugar, and sometimes nuts or raisins.
Without frosting, the roll showcases the natural flavors of the dough and spice.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain dough provides dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Cinnamon is rich in polyphenols, which may help reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports blood sugar balance
items.content: Some studies suggest cinnamon can aid in stabilizing blood glucose levels.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates in the dough supply fast‑acting energy, making it a convenient morning snack.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough contains B1, B2, and B3 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The sweet filling can raise the calorie count and affect blood sugar.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional dough contains wheat, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Butter and sugar make the roll calorie‑rich, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Excess cinnamon
items.content: Large amounts of cinnamon may irritate the stomach in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the roll warm, sliced in half. It pairs well with coffee, tea, or milk. For extra richness, add a pat of butter or a sprinkle of nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Warm before serving in the oven or microwave.
